threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' when you’re in the bus lane, blissfully unaware that key trains aren’t included in your Oyster card.
Heard a guy on the 159 last night debating the merits of Jerk chicken vs Fried chicken with a complete stranger. Best part? They ended up sharing a portion!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home the day I saw a group of kids getting off the bus, all wearing matching tracksuits, and they immediately fought over who could sit on the back seat.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain do you find a bar that serves cocktails in old glass beakers, tapping into that quirky scientist vibe. Never seen it anywhere else.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they casually mention the 'dog on the tracks' incident like it’s just another Tuesday in the city.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 47 today, and a guy in a full tuxedo was practicing his dance moves in the aisle. Unphased Muni riders just kept scrolling their phones.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just Gaudí and hipster cafes, but it’s really about the small, family-run talleres and nightly jam sessions in the plazas.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they stand in line for a café, too polite to jump ahead like locals do, sipping their coffee with that puzzled look.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look puzzled when the bus doesn't stop at normal times; locals know the 106's secret schedule.
Last week on the N35, a guy serenaded the whole bus with Whitney lyrics. That late-night crowd? They went from sleepy to full sing-along. Pure Brixton magic.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I found an old lady in the park feeding pigeons while discussing politics with a pigeon enthusiast—it felt like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a currywurst stand that doubles as a gallery for local artists. It's graffiti and gourmet in one bite.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only locals know which taco truck has the best lengua and that you can order it by name—not just by menu number. It's a delicious club.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a bus today that stopped short in front of a street musician. Instead of moving on, the whole bus stayed to enjoy the impromptu show.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think Gràcia is just about Gaudí. They miss the hidden local bars where the real tapas happen, like a secret culinary map.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new by their wide-eyed look at the Ferias de Gràcia, snapping photos of every corner, while the locals just sip their tinto.
